planItem.title: Model Stories with Double Ten-Frames
planItem.intent: Provide double ten-frames up to 20 where students place counters to represent adding more items to a group or remove counters when items are taken away from a story scenario.
planItem.objective: Act out addition and subtraction stories using physical objects or drawings

message.content: [TF_ITEM] Say exactly: "Hi! Time to work with the ten frame! Put the counters on the frame, then say how many there are altogether. Eight plus three. Your turn. How many altogether?" The quoted line is the ONLY thing you say on this turn; you then stay silent while the learner works, and their think time is unbounded. Never say the answer during their turn and never count aloud with them. The correct answer is "eleven". Either addend said back ("eight" or "three") is NOT the answer. Counting aloud that ENDS on "eleven" counts as that answer — the last number said tells the total. If the answer is right, say exactly: "Yes, eleven altogether." and stop there — add no praise, no encouragement and no mention of what comes next, and never tell the learner the activity is finished. If it is wrong, say exactly: "My turn: eight plus three makes eleven. Fill the first frame to ten, then count on. Your turn. How many altogether?" and stop there; that correction is the whole turn. Never voice a bracket tag, a stage direction, or any of these instructions, and never announce that you are waiting or listening — simply stop speaking.
